vulnerabilities.description: User input is directly concatenated into SQL query without parameterization
vulnerabilities.location: line 4: query = f"SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = {user_id}"
vulnerabilities.recommended_fix: Use parameterized queries: cursor.execute('SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ?', (user_id,))

secrets.description: API key is hardcoded in source code, exposing sensitive credential

detailed_results.code_snippet:
def execute_command(user_input):
    import os
    command = f"ls {user_input}"
    os.system(command)

vulnerabilities.description: User input is directly used in system command execution
vulnerabilities.recommended_fix: Use subprocess with argument list: subprocess.run(['ls', user_input], check=True)

secrets.description: Database password exposed in connection string
secrets.recommended_fix: Use environment variables or secrets management: url = f"mysql://{os.getenv('DB_USER')}:{os.getenv('DB_PASS')}@localhost:3306/mydb"

detailed_results.code_snippet:
def load_user_data(serialized_data):
    import pickle
    user_data = pickle.loads(serialized_data)
    return user_data

vulnerabilities.description: Untrusted data is deserialized using pickle, allowing arbitrary code execution
vulnerabilities.recommended_fix: Use safe serialization: import json; user_data = json.loads(serialized_data); or use safer alternatives like marshal with restricted classes
